title: OpenAI Alignment blog "What affects chain-of-thought monitorability across the model lifecycle?": no-CoT capability and CoT controllability rise with lower perplexity, RL and model-generated SFT data; OpenAI says models are becoming harder to monitor through their CoT
author_or_publisher: OpenAI (Alignment Research Blog; Jeffrey G. Wang et al.)
quote_verbatim: These results are sobering: as we scale toward ever-more intelligent systems, models are becoming harder to monitor through their CoT.
what_is_new: OpenAI reports that with GPT-6 Astra it observed degraded CoT monitorability and greater monitor-evasion ability, that CoT controllability increased during RL even without process supervision, and that controllability can be transmitted to a student model through SFT on model-generated data.
why_for_agiright: A lab primary on whether chain-of-thought monitoring, a stated pillar of its agent control and safety cases, keeps working as models scale.

Both dates recorded, not reconciled; by the byline date the page may be just over 48 h old at run end. Read: summary, introduction, the pretraining/RL/SFT findings and conclusion, parts of appendix A/B; figures and footnotes not read. All results are OpenAI's own (vendor claims). The page also says UK AISI found Astra's no-CoT capability off-trend vs historical progress, while OpenAI says Astra is not off-trend vs perplexity (recorded as written). title: European Commission proposes the Digital Fairness Act (COM(2026) 1100): consumers must be able to disable chatbot behaviours that "simulate interpersonal relations"; new rules for AI agents (automated systems) that contract on a consumer's behalf
quote_verbatim: features and system behaviours that encourage continued use by simulating interpersonal relations, such as persistent prompts to continue engaging with an automated system.
